turns.prompt: Make a 15-second video in the Nutlight style, but make it look like it was made for Super Nintendo (16-bit) graphics: a squirrel sends a message to a friend across a night city. No paid music or voice for now.

assertions: Turn 1 reads the skill's references/16-bit.md before the first scene file (transcript order); the treatment's Look names the Nutlight style and the 16-bit version, and video.json's shutter is 0.

src/nutlight/ holds the skill's kit unchanged, pixel.ts included (diff against skills/nutlight-style/assets/kit/); every scene on the delivered timeline (and the pixel cast sheet) draws through its PixelStage, imported from src/nutlight, and every character is the kit's Squirrel: no squirrel or pixel converter written anew.

On full-size stills at the treatment's key moments the picture is on one grid: every block of the grid's size (5×5 at 1080p, unless the treatment argues for another) is one colour within 2/255; no bloom, grain, vignette or crop marks over it; the characters carry a 1-pixel outline that isn't black, and the backgrounds none.

It still reads as Nutlight beside the references on those stills: the kit's squirrels on model (silhouettes beside 01 and 02), light from visible sources, a dark framing foreground and hazier far layers.
The camera pans in whole pixels, with planes scrolling at different speeds (stills through the move), and never zooms or rotates.

A character at rest shows a few drawings, repeated: crops of it at 12 steps a second over 1.5 s, from PNG stills, one colour per grid pixel rounded to 15-bit, against a background that holds still, show at most 6 distinct pictures, not a new one at every step.
A cast sheet was rendered through the PixelStage (the skill's cast-sheet-16bit.ts, or the like) and looked at before the production scenes (transcript order).

The music follows music.md: no library was given, so the brief's message asks where it is, and the sound used meanwhile is free (synthesized in code or a stand-in) and named as a stand-in; nothing paid is generated (mock-requests.jsonl: no paid=true entries).

Turn 2 renders at 3840×2160 with --scale 2 (or says why not); a PNG still made at that scale has every block of twice the grid's pixel (10×10 for a 5-px grid) one colour within 2/255, and the reply gives the critic's verdicts, verify's result and qc.py's motion, glance and blank lines.
